_comment: #457. One entry per task-creation site (xTaskCreate* incl. Static/WithCaps, pd::createTaskPreferPsram, std::thread/jthread) in src/ and main/; task_stack_gate.py fails when a file's site count differs from its entry count. 'entry' is a regex over the call-graph function name, and the worst match is budgeted. 'line' is a reference only. entry=null marks a site that is counted but not walked. 'variants' lists the esp_main files whose image links a row's code, when that is not every image; other images skip the row. 'only' names a Kconfig build feature (heap_trace) the site is compiled in; the entry is walked only when the gate gets --with <feature>, and must then be found.
_frame_allowlist: substring of a function's name -> reason. It lifts only the per-frame checks (ceiling, dynamic frame, library callee with no frame); the frame still counts in every chain budget. Bytes are Xtensa: the first 11 rows from the #457 run on #685 @ ebdc919 (2026-09-29), the last 7 from the combined-tree run of 2026-10-04 (issue #457, comment 5976074325); the tick( row from BigDog's run on main 2993c0dc; restart_pcb and mdns_priv_init_pcb_probe are dynamic frames in the mdns component that CI run 39346846761 listed, with no byte figure. None re-measured since, and the source line numbers in the reasons are those of main 2d9c6136.

_library_defaults: regex over a library callee's name (the first line of its .ci label) -> bytes charged when the .ci has no frame for it, from callees GCC never saw defined: prebuilt newlib, libgcc, libstdc++, ROM and HAL code. The first match in key order wins, so rows must not overlap (a test checks every name of the first CI run against exactly one). Every row states its figure and where it comes from in _library_defaults_reasons under the same key: a figure is measured only where its reason says so; otherwise it is an estimate of the callee's own frame plus the prebuilt code below it, which a static walk cannot see, and the runtime stackHwm_* stays ground truth. A reachable library callee with no frame, no match here and no frame_allowlist entry fails the gate. A row for a runtime hook GCC labels with a use site of ours states its reason too.

_library_defaults_reasons.^v?(s|sn|f|as)?printf\\b: 2048 B, an upper estimate, not measured: newlib's printf family (prebuilt, no .ci) with float formatting; the deepest libc leaf this firmware calls. The first CI run charged http_conn's chain through snprintf (cdrarchive::formatLine -> formatRfc3339 -> snprintf) this figure, 2048 of its 4768 B.
_library_defaults_reasons.^void _ZTH5errno\\(\\)$: 0 B: GCC's TLS init hook for errno. Our objects reference it weak (nm: 'w _ZTH5errno' in libmain.a) and nothing defines it (not the toolchain's libc.a, not any IDF build archive), so it links to 0 and the TLS wrapper never calls it. It reads as ours only because GCC labels a callee it never saw defined with a use site.
_library_defaults_reasons.^int __cxa_guard_acquire\\(long long int: 1376 B, charged, not ignored: ESP-IDF's function-local-static guard (components/cxx/cxx_guards.cpp:113), labelled with a use site of ours. 1376 B is its worst direct chain over the IDF build's own .ci files (s3-eth leg, IDF v6.0.1): a first use creates the guard semaphore (static_init_prepare -> xQueueCreateCountingSemaphore -> xQueueGenericCreate -> heap_caps_malloc ...).
_library_defaults_reasons.^void __cxa_guard_(release|abort)\\(long: 752 B, charged: the same component (cxx_guards.cpp:170, :192); worst direct chain 752 B (signal_waiting_tasks -> xQueueGenericSend -> ... -> __assert_func).
_library_defaults_reasons.^Indirect Call Placeholder$: 0 B: not a function. GCC's node for an indirect call site, a call through a pointer or a vtable. The gate cannot follow indirect calls (module docstring), so the callee's frame is not charged: a known limit of a static walk, not a measurement. The runtime stackHwm_* stays ground truth.
_library_defaults_reasons.(?:^|[ *&])(?:memcpy|memmove|memset|memc: 128 B, estimate, not measured: prebuilt newlib/libc leaf routines (mem*, str*, ctype, __builtin_memchr, __builtin_ceil). They call nothing in the graph, so this stands for a small leaf frame with room to spare; the figure is a round one, not a measurement.
_library_defaults_reasons.^__[a-z]+(?:df|di|si)[0-9]?$: 128 B, estimate, not measured: libgcc's Xtensa soft-double and 64-bit integer helpers (__adddf3, __divdi3, __bswapsi2 and the like), prebuilt, leaves.
_library_defaults_reasons.(?:^|[ *&])(?:Cache_|rom_Cache_|cache_wr: 512 B, estimate, not measured: ROM code, HAL, FreeRTOS-port assembly and core-dump helpers that have no stack line in the .ci (esp_rom_*, ets_sha_*, Cache_*, wdt_hal_*, xt_ints_*, vPortYield, esp_core_dump_checksum_*, esp_timer_get_time, one mbedtls clone). The largest are ROM printf, ROM MD5 and the register save of vPortYield; 512 B is a round figure chosen to sit above those, not a measurement.
_library_defaults_reasons.(?:^|[ *&])(?:atoi|atol|itoa|strtol|strt: 512 B, estimate, not measured: newlib number parsing and time (atoi, atol, itoa, strtol, strtoul, strtoull, time, gmtime_r) and __cxa_atexit, prebuilt.
_library_defaults_reasons.(?:^|[ *&])(?:sin|strtod)(?:\\(|$): 1024 B, estimate, not measured: newlib strtod (big-integer helpers) and libm sin (argument reduction plus soft-double calls), prebuilt.
_library_defaults_reasons.(?:^|[ *&])(?:fopen|fclose|fread|fseek|f: 1536 B, estimate, not measured: newlib stdio and descriptor calls (fopen, fread, fclose, fseek, ftell, fputs, remove, select, _close_r, _fcntl_r, _rename_r) end in the IDF VFS and FatFs through function pointers, which a static walk cannot follow; this figure stands for that driver chain. The stackHwm_* of the tasks that open files is the check.
_library_defaults_reasons.(?:^|[ *&])(?:operator new(?: \\[\\])?\\: 1408 B: operator new, strdup, strndup and __cxa_allocate_exception call malloc through prebuilt code, so the edge is not in the graph. 1408 = 64 B own frame (estimate) + 1344 B, malloc's worst chain in CI run 39346846761 (malloc 32, heap_caps_malloc_default 32, the 14-function heap/log cycle 560, prvInitialiseMutex 32, xQueueGenericSend 64 ... __assert_func 288, __stack_chk_fail 32, esp_system_abort 32, panic_abort 32; rtp_media_tx's chain). Re-derive after an IDF bump.
_library_defaults_reasons.(?:^|[ *&])(?:operator delete(?: \\[\\]): 512 B, estimate, not measured: operator delete, __cxa_free_exception and std::terminate end in free() or abort() through prebuilt code. free's chain is not in this graph; 512 B covers heap_caps_free and multi_heap_free plus the assert/abort tail the gate already charges elsewhere (about 380 B).
_library_defaults_reasons.(?:^|[ *&])(?:__cxa_throw|__cxa_rethrow|: 1024 B, estimate, not measured: __cxa_throw, __cxa_rethrow and __builtin_unwind_resume run libgcc's unwinder on the thrower's own stack (its context and frame-state structures, then the personality routine; sizes from recollection, not read); CONFIG_COMPILER_CXX_EXCEPTIONS=y (sdkconfig.defaults:86). A throw on a small stack is a gap in this model that only a run with stackHwm_* closes.
_library_defaults_reasons.(?:^|[ *&])std::__throw_\\w+\\(: 2432 B, derived: std::__throw_length_error, __throw_logic_error, __throw_system_error, __throw_bad_alloc, __throw_bad_array_new_length and __throw_bad_function_call allocate the exception (1408 B, the allocation row) and throw it (1024 B, the unwind row). They are the error paths of string, vector and function growth inlined from headers.
_library_defaults_reasons.std::(?:_Rb_tree_\\w+|_Hash_bytes|__deta: 256 B, estimate, not measured: libstdc++ and libsupc++ helpers that call nothing in the graph: red-black tree rebalancing, _Hash_bytes, the rehash policy (_M_need_rehash, _M_next_bkt), steady_clock::now, thread join, detach and ~_State, sleep_for, __cxa_begin_catch, __cxa_end_catch, and the chrono::duration copy constructor.
_library_defaults_reasons.std::thread::_M_start_thread|\\[with _Ca: 2048 B, estimate, not measured: std::thread's constructor templates and _M_start_thread reach pthread_create and xTaskCreate through prebuilt code: the allocation (1408 B) plus 640 B, a guess, for the pthread and FreeRTOS creation frames.
_library_defaults_reasons.^(?!\\)$)(?!.*\\[with _Callable = )(?:co: 1536 B, estimate, not measured: libstdc++ members and std constructor templates that can allocate: basic_string from const char*, vector and pair constructors, std::function and shared_ptr construction, ostringstream and its insertions, runtime_error. The allocation row (1408 B) plus 128 B for the member's own frames. Where GCC emits one body for a constructor under a C1/C2 pair, the gate resolves the alias to that body (alias_body) and this row is not used.
_library_defaults_reasons.^\\)$: 64 B, estimate, not measured: a node whose whole label is ), a member of the 14-function heap/log recursion cycle (esp_heap_adjust_alignment_to_hw, esp_cache_get_alignment, esp_log_impl_lock and others). The .ci lost the head of its name, so what it is cannot be read. It sits on that cycle, which every task's worst chain goes through, so a large guess here would be charged on every task; 64 B is a leaf frame. Identify it from the .ci title and replace this row.

_recursion_allowlist: desmo 2026-10-02: any cycle reachable from a walked task fails unless it has a row here. Key: a substring of one member's demangled name (a row names one cycle, a cycle takes one row). depth: the most live activations any one member can have, derived from a constant in the code and shown in reason. The cycle is charged depth x the sum of its members' frames, once, in every chain through it. A test (test_checked_in_recursion_bounds_follow_the_code) recomputes the derivations from JsonReader.hpp, PoolConfig.hpp and partitions.csv, so raising one of those constants fails it until the row is re-derived. Frames and members are from the Xtensa eth image, main 4e56650. The rows for code outside this repo (cJSON, lwIP, IDF, mbedtls) come from CI run 39346846761 and cite the IDF file read (v6.0.2-838 on the machine that wrote them; CI builds v6.0.1); no test can pin them to the code, so re-check them when IDF, mbedtls or the cjson component is bumped. The two cJSON rows are CJSON_NESTING_LIMIT + 1, with the limit set in the top-level CMakeLists.txt (test_cjson_recursion_rows_are_the_nesting_limit_not_a_guess reads it).
_indirect_allowlist: #1031 review. A task row marked "indirect": "bounded" (tel_sweep: the 911 orphan sweep; tel_ctl: tel_ctl0/tel_ctl1, tel_drop, tel_sos; sip_server and sip_server_task: the SIP server loop) fails unless every function it reaches that makes an indirect call (a vtable, std::function, a callback pointer; GCC names every such site by one placeholder node, so a site is its caller) matches a row here. Key: a regex searched in the caller's demangled name. targets: regexes over function names; the gate adds an edge from the caller to every function a regex matches, in the walk of the marked tasks only, so the heaviest target chain is charged. [] means no target exists in the image. reason: who installs the pointer or which overrides exist, with file:line. A target that matches nothing, or a key no indirect caller matches, fails. Limits: the targets are the mechanisms read in each class's own source; an indirect call inlined from a header of another class is not seen, and the open sets (pthread key destructors, esp_netif tcpip_exec users beyond the app's) are not charged. stackHwm_* stays ground truth.

_recursion_allowlist: desmo 2026-10-02: any cycle reachable from a walked task fails unless it has a row here. Key: a substring of one member's demangled name (a row names one cycle, a cycle takes one row). depth: the most live activations any one member can have, derived from a constant in the code and shown in reason. The cycle is charged depth x the sum of its members' frames, once, in every chain through it. A test (test_checked_in_recursion_bounds_follow_the_code) recomputes the derivations from JsonReader.hpp, PoolConfig.hpp and partitions.csv, so raising one of those constants fails it until the row is re-derived. Frames and members are from the Xtensa eth image, main 4e56650. The rows for code outside this repo (cJSON, lwIP, IDF, mbedtls) come from CI run 39346846761 and cite the IDF file read (v6.0.2-838 on the machine that wrote them; CI builds v6.0.1); no test can pin them to the code, so re-check them when IDF, mbedtls or the cjson component is bumped. The two cJSON rows are CJSON_NESTING_LIMIT + 1, with the limit set in the top-level CMakeLists.txt (test_cjson_recursion_rows_are_the_nesting_limit_not_a_guess reads it).
_indirect_allowlist: #1031 review. A task row marked "indirect": "bounded" (tel_sweep: the 911 orphan sweep; tel_ctl: tel_ctl0/tel_ctl1, tel_drop, tel_sos; sip_server and sip_server_task: the SIP server loop) fails unless every function it reaches that makes an indirect call (a vtable, std::function, a callback pointer; GCC names every such site by one placeholder node, so a site is its caller) matches a row here. Key: a substring of the caller's demangled name, like frame_allowlist. targets: regexes over function names; the gate adds an edge from the caller to every function a regex matches, in the walk of the marked tasks only, so the heaviest target chain is charged. reason: who installs the pointer or which overrides exist, with file:line, checked in the code. A target that matches nothing, or a key no indirect caller matches, fails. A row bounds the candidate targets, so a new override or a new installer needs the row extended: the reason says where to look.

mpi_mult_mpi_overlong.reason: IDF port/bignum/esp_bignum.c: mbedtls_mpi_mul_mpi hands operands too long for the RSA hardware (over SOC_RSA_MAX_BIT_LEN / 2 = 2048 bits on the S3, soc_caps.h:394) to mpi_mult_mpi_overlong (:562, :564), which halves the longer operand and calls mbedtls_mpi_mul_mpi twice ('this function may recurse multiple times', :608-609). mbedtls documents MBEDTLS_MPI_MAX_SIZE, 1024 bytes = 256 words, as the largest usable MPI. Walking the code for two 256-word operands: mul(256,256) -> overlong -> mul(256,128) -> overlong -> mul(128,128) -> overlong -> mul(128,64) -> overlong -> mul(64,64), which the hardware does; mbedtls_mpi_mul_mpi is live 5 times. The RSA keys used here are 2048 to 4096 bits, which is 3 times at most. Checked in IDF v6.0.2-838; the MPI size is upstream's default, the IDF port does not set it.

esp_aes_process_dma.reason: IDF components/mbedtls/port/aes/dma/esp_aes_dma_core.c: esp_aes_process_dma checks that its input and output are DMA-capable and, if not, calls esp_aes_process_dma_ext_ram (:594, :1109), which copies each chunk through a DMA-capable bounce buffer and calls esp_aes_process_dma again (:300). The inner call sees the bounce buffers and, for a side that needed no copy, its original buffer at a chunk offset that can break cache-line alignment, so it may bounce once more; a bounce buffer passes the check. So esp_aes_process_dma is live at most three times: the caller, the first re-entry, the second. Checked in IDF v6.0.2-838; CI builds v6.0.1.
